entries.meaning: To cook meat slowly in a covered pot with a little liquid. ---
examples: Braise the short ribs for three hours.
We braised the lamb in red wine.
The beef has been braising all afternoon.

entries.meaning: To brown the surface of meat quickly over very high heat. ---
examples: Sear the steak hard on both sides.
She seared the scallops in a smoking pan.
The chef has already seared the roast.
entries.русский: обжаривать на сильном огне, подрумянивать до корочки

entries.meaning: To cook food slowly outdoors over smoke or hot coals. ---
examples: They barbecue every Fourth of July.
We barbecued ribs all afternoon.
He is barbecuing chicken in the backyard.
entries.русский: жарить на барбекю, готовить на углях
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (barbecue ribs), intransitive (they barbecue every weekend)
entries.contrast: Spelled barbecue (short form BBQ); barbeque is nonstandard. The -e drops before -ing: barbecuing.

entries.meaning: To cook the surface of food until it turns brown. ---
examples: Brown the beef before you add the tomatoes.
I browned the butter until it smelled nutty.
The crust is browning nicely.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (brown the beef), intransitive (the crust is browning)

entries.meaning: To cook sugar, or the sugar in a food, until it turns brown and sweet. ---
examples: Slow heat will caramelize the onions.
She caramelized the sugar for the flan.
The shallots have caramelized beautifully.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (caramelize the sugar), intransitive (the onions caramelized)
entries.contrast: American English spells it -ize; British English uses caramelise.

entries.meaning: To boil vegetables briefly and then drop them into cold water. ---
examples: Blanch the green beans for two minutes.
I blanched the tomatoes to loosen their skins.
The spinach has already been blanched.

entries.meaning: To spoon juices or melted fat over food while it roasts. ---
examples: Baste the turkey every half hour.
He basted the chicken with herb butter.
She has been basting the roast all morning.
entries.русский: поливать соком или жиром при жарке

entries.meaning: To beat eggs together and cook them in a pan while stirring. ---
examples: I'll scramble a couple of eggs.
He scrambled six eggs for the three of us.
She is scrambling eggs with cheese and chives.

entries.meaning: To pass flour or sugar through a fine mesh to remove the lumps. ---
examples: Sift the flour and the baking powder together.
I sifted powdered sugar over the cake.
The dry ingredients have all been sifted.

entries.meaning: To put two or more ingredients together. ---
examples: Combine the wet and the dry ingredients.
I combined the two sauces into one.
Once the eggs have been combined with the sugar, add the flour.

entries.meaning: To move a liquid around in a circle, or to move that way. ---
examples: Swirl the pan to coat it with butter.
He swirled the wine in his glass.
Cream was swirling through the black coffee.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (swirl the pan), intransitive (cream swirled through the coffee)

entries.meaning: To make a liquid thicker, or to become thicker. ---
examples: A spoonful of flour will thicken the gravy.
The sauce thickened as it cooled.
The stew has thickened nicely.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (thicken the gravy), intransitive (the sauce thickened)

entries.meaning: To make something soft, or to become soft. ---
examples: Let the butter soften on the counter.
I softened the onions in oil first.
The raisins have softened in the hot water.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (soften the butter), intransitive (let it soften)
entries.contrast: The t is silent: SAW-fun, not SOFT-un.

entries.meaning: To flavor and preserve food by hanging it in smoke. ---
examples: They smoke their own brisket out back.
We smoked the ribs for six hours.
The trout has been smoked over applewood.

entries.meaning: To spread butter or oil on a pan so that food will not stick. ---
examples: Grease the pan before you pour in the batter.
I greased two cake tins.
The baking sheet has already been greased.

entries.meaning: To coat food with a shiny liquid such as syrup or thin icing. ---
examples: Glaze the ham with brown sugar and mustard.
She glazed the donuts while they were warm.
The carrots have been glazed in butter and honey.

entries.meaning: To spread a thick sweet icing over a cake. ---
examples: Let the cake cool before you frost it.
She frosted the cupcakes with buttercream.
The layer cake has been frosted and decorated.
entries.contrast: Americans frost a cake; the British ice it. The sweet topping itself is frosting.

entries.meaning: To arrange food in flat layers, one on top of another. ---
examples: Layer the noodles, the sauce, and the cheese.
She layered the potatoes in a buttered dish.
I am layering the trifle now.

entries.meaning: To keep food somewhere until it is needed. ---
examples: Store the flour in an airtight container.
We stored the apples in the basement.
The cookies are being stored in the freezer.

entries.meaning: To change sugar into alcohol or acid through the action of yeast or bacteria. ---
examples: Let the dough ferment overnight.
The cabbage fermented for three weeks.
The wine has been fermenting since October.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (ferment the cabbage), intransitive (the dough fermented)
entries.contrast: The verb is stressed on the second syllable, fur-MENT; the noun is FUR-ment.

entries.meaning: To cook meat or fruit slowly in liquid in a covered pot. ---
examples: Stew the lamb with onions and carrots.
She stewed apples for the pie filling.
The beef has been stewing for three hours.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (stew the lamb), intransitive (the beef is stewing)
entries.contrast: General American drops the y-sound: STOO, not STYOO.

entries.meaning: To dip food quickly into a liquid. ---
examples: Dunk the cookie in your milk.
He dunked the bread in the olive oil.
She is dunking fries into her milkshake.
entries.contrast: Dunk something in or into a liquid.

entries.meaning: To become ripe and ready to eat, or to make fruit ripe.
examples: Tomatoes ripen fast on a sunny windowsill.
The avocados ripened in a paper bag.
The peaches have all ripened at once.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (a paper bag ripens pears), intransitive (the fruit ripened)
